title.narrative: Share-Net Jordan Hub

description.narrative: Share-Net Jordan Hub Share-Net Jordan hosted by the Higher Population Council since 2016. The intended impact of this knowledge hub is to encourage the sharing of knowledge and information in the field of SRH&RR and the translation of research into policy and practice, by supporting and advocating for an enabling environment for research development, implementation and uptake of knowledge that will inform reproductive health policies, practices and programs through an iterative cycle of evidence informed decision making (managing the research agenda, producing and synthesizing evidence, promoting use of evidence, decision making for policies and practice, SRH policies programs and practice) to improve the SRH and reproductive rights status of Jordanian citizens.The knowledge hub aims to fulfill the following objectives:1.To create a dynamic online platform on SRH and reproductive rights in Jordan for all stakeholders in the sector2.To facilitate knowledge generation and dissemination of SRH&RR issues both through online and offline engagement3.To build capacity of key stakeholders on identified knowledge gaps on SRH&RR issues in JordanTo achieve these objectives the knowledge hub will:•Stimulate the sharing of existing knowledge among platform participants, the generation of new knowledge to address prioritized research area gaps.•Translate knowledge into formats appropriate for intended audiences, so as to contribute to the application of knowledge in the field of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Reproductive Rights (SRH &RR) in line with the international reporting obligations to effectively inform on SDGs.•Direct funding into SRH&RR priorities.•Build synergies among different stakeholders, partners, projects and programs.•Identify the most effective methods for facilitating uptake of evidence in policy and practice.•Stimulate an informed national sexual and reproductive health reproductive rights policy debate.Share Net Jordan VisionPeople have the right to access high-quality health services and the ability to make informed decisions on their sexual and reproductive healthShare Net Jordan MissionTo strengthen linkages between research, policy and practice through sharing, generating, translating and promoting the use of knowledge for the development of better policies and practices in SRH&RR

comment.narrative: Share-Net Jordan and the Higher Population Council have partnered with Gender and Adolescence: Global Evidence (GAGE) to strengthen the evidence base on gender and adolescence. This collaboration aims to improve the lives of adolescents, especially those vulnerable, by sharing knowledge and findings from the GAGE Programme with practitioners and policymakers in Jordan. The partnership, running from August 2023 to March 2026, focuses on establishing new national partnerships and enhancing collaboration through information sharing, expertise provision, advocacy, and stakeholder engagement.

The Summary of the Interviews After interviewing selected members of the Community of Practice (CoP) the members thoughtfully suggested that the strategies to maintain a lively atmosphere and keep members engaged lie in fostering interactive workshops where participants can share personal experiences and ideas in a welcoming environment. They also emphasized the value of having a clear work plan for the CoP and clearly defined responsibilities for each participant to create a dynamic and productive setting. To improve the facilitation of Share-Net, members proposed offering more tailored training sessions and creating smaller, focused groups for in-depth discussions on specific topics, which would encourage meaningful dialogue. They recommended enhancing communication and actively gathering feedback to shape activities according to the members� needs, ensuring that everyone�s voice is included. Additionally, they suggested providing more opportunities for members to take the lead on initiatives and incorporating an evaluation system within the CoP to enhance its overall effectiveness. These thoughtful suggestions reflect the commitment of members to create a vibrant and impactful community.Summary of the survey results Insights from the 2024 Share-Net Jordan (SNJ) CoP survey shed light on member perceptions and experiences. Many participants highlighted a strong sense of community, noting that their engagement significantly boosted their skills and positively influenced their work. Members appreciated the CoPs as a respectful space for addressing key issues, promoting collaboration, and sparking timely discussions. Additionally, most respondents felt that their participation led to the creation of knowledge that extended beyond the SNJ network, enriching wider community involvement. However, opinions were mixed regarding the sufficiency of funding for activities, pointing to a potential area for improvement.

The representatives of the Community of Practice (CoP) underscore the significance of consistent communication and active member involvement as fundamental to the success of the community. They advocate for the simplification of work processes to encourage broader participation and stress the need for flexibility in adding members to the CoP as the need arises. The representatives emphasize the critical importance of members' genuine interest and willingness to work collaboratively, viewing it as essential for the CoP's effectiveness. Regular reminders of the CoP's overarching goals are deemed necessary to keep all members focused and on track. Furthermore, the representatives highlight the value of enhanced networking with related SN members, promoting face-to-face activities over online ones when possible. Time management is recognized as crucial, ensuring members have adequate time for CoP activities. A designated focal point with authority between the CoP and SN is recommended for streamlined communication, and the representatives stress the mandatory attendance of all members at the first meeting, recognizing its impactful role in establishing a strong foundation for collaborative efforts.

The semi-structured interviews with representatives of the Communities of Practice (CoPs) provided insights into their current status and ways to enhance them. It was suggested to foster personal relationships by increasing opportunities for in-person meetings and collaboration beyond shared interests. The involvement of Share-Net Jordan coordinators and continuous motivation of CoP members were proposed to keep the CoPs active. The impact of COVID-19 on online communication was acknowledged, with an expectation of returning to in-person meetings. The questionnaire measuring CoP effectiveness revealed positive feedback, indicating improved competencies, a respectful atmosphere, and the influence of CoPs on actions. Dissemination of knowledge beyond the capital region was highlighted, suggesting workshops in other areas and diverse knowledge-sharing tools. Overall, the CoPs were recognized for addressing relevant topics, striving for high-quality outputs, and improving work, with appreciation expressed for the Share-Net Jordan team's efforts.

The success stories highlight the collective efforts of individuals and organizations committed to advancing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Reproductive Rights (SRH&RR). Through initiatives like the launch of SHIRIM products facilitated by Monther Karajeh and Sana Salem's integration of SRH&RR resources into counseling, SNJ's impact is evident. Wafa Zenateieh's journalistic endeavors to combat misinformation and Dr. Abdullah Hanatleh's utilization of SNJ insights in organizational procedures further underscore the multifaceted influence of SNJ in promoting holistic well-being and advancing SRH&RR initiatives.
